Consult Summary:
- Telemedicine consult for a male patient with 3 days of non-bloody diarrhea, midline abdominal pain, and one episode of vomiting; presentation most consistent with acute gastroenteritis; supportive care advised with in-person GP review if worsening or not improving.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Diarrhea for ~3 days with abdominal pain and one episode of vomiting today.
- Symptom details:
  - Diarrhea: Frequent, urgent bowel movements with sensation of needing to go again immediately after (tenesmus). Non-bloody. Interfering with ability to work; needs to stay near a toilet.
  - Abdominal pain: Central/infra-umbilical; mild; improves somewhat after bowel movements; patient notes audible bowel sounds.
  - Nausea/vomiting: Nausea today; vomited after morning fruit; no blood in emesis (red color attributed to strawberries).
  - Hydration/Intake: Likely suboptimal fluid intake; limiting food due to frequent stools.
  - Fever: No clear fever; reports some sweating over last ~4 days; uncertain about temperature.
  - Other: Pain mildly increased with self-palpation. No chest pain. Able to walk and talk but staying home due to toilet needs.
- Timeline: Acute onset 3 days ago; symptoms neither improving nor clearly worsening.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Eating seems to increase toilet frequency; abdominal pain improves after bowel movements.
- Pertinent negatives (reported): No visible blood in stool; no blood in vomit; no new breathing issues beyond baseline asthma.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma (uses inhaler; no acute exacerbation reported during this illness).
- No other chronic conditions reported.

Medications:
- Asthma inhaler (brand recently changed): dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies (NKDA).

Social History:
- Employed; currently staying home due to symptoms.
- Reports being a foreign national.
- Suspects not drinking enough water.
- Tobacco/alcohol/substance use: Not recorded.
- Recent travel/exposures/sick contacts: Not recorded.

Family History:
- Father died of bowel (colorectal) cancer approximately 10 years ago.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Examination findings: Telehealth only. Patient reports mild central abdominal tenderness with self-palpation. Speaking comfortably; ambulatory. No blood in stool; last emesis this morning after eating fruit.

Investigations:
- None ordered; no results available.

Assessment & Plan:
- Overall Impression:
  - Acute gastroenteritis (likely viral) causing non-bloody diarrhea, crampy infra-umbilical abdominal pain, and a single emesis; currently without red-flag features on history.

- DDx Integration (brief):
  - Acute viral gastroenteritis: Supports—acute 3-day course, nausea/vomiting, non-bloody diarrhea, crampy pain relieved by bowel movements; Opposes—symptoms not clearly improving yet.
  - Acute bacterial gastroenteritis (foodborne): Supports—acute diarrhea with cramps; Opposes—no blood or high fever.
  - IBS-D (functional): Supports—pain relief after defecation, urgency; Opposes—acute onset with vomiting favors infection over functional disorder.

- Issue 1: Acute diarrhea with abdominal pain and nausea/vomiting (suspected infectious gastroenteritis)
  - Plan:
    - Increase oral fluid intake as able.
    - Monitor for fever; if a temperature develops or symptoms worsen, seek in-person GP assessment for abdominal examination.
    - Stay home until symptoms improve.
    - Avoid antibiotics at this time per clinician advice.
    - Follow-up: Patient plans to wait ~1 day; if not improving, will book an in-person GP appointment.

- Issue 2: Asthma, stable
  - Assessment: No new respiratory symptoms beyond baseline; inhaler brand recently changed. Clinician advised inhaler is very unlikely to cause current GI symptoms.
  - Plan: No change discussed.

- Issue 3: Family history of colorectal cancer (father)
  - Assessment: Current presentation most consistent with acute infection; less likely related to colorectal cancer.
  - Plan: Reassurance provided. If symptoms persist, discuss further evaluation with GP.

- General plan items:
  - Return/seek care sooner if significant worsening.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: No vital signs recorded; no specific medication names or dosing; stool frequency not quantified; travel/sick contacts not documented.  
● Conflicts: Reported DOB/year vs age inconsistent (patient stated 1990 DOB and “48 years old”)—conflict noted.  
● Transcript quality: Some incomplete/unclear statements; overall history sufficient for assessment.
